learning: Iteration 7 showed s-bend steering_oscillation at 0.347, so the damping margin is shrinking as the track narrows. Check whether slalom oscillation stays at or below about 0.32 with kd 0.65, whether slalom finishes rise above 15/20, and whether slalom off_track cases now have max_error below 0.06. If oscillation still rises, the track should return toward 0.11 m. If max_error stays near 0.034 with off_track endings, turn response is the limit and wheel_track is the next lever.
notes: Applies the Builder's wheel_track step to 0.105 m. kd rises from 0.60 to 0.65 to damp the faster turn response, while kp, ki, base_speed and sensing stay unchanged so the geometry effect remains readable.
rationale: Iteration 7 (score 889.3) is the best design. Oval and s-bend both finish 20/20, and slalom finishes 15/20 with off_track endings at max_error near 0.034. The Builder's iteration 8 changes wheel_track from 0.11 to 0.105 m and keeps every other geometry field fixed. Narrowing the track raises turn rate per unit of wheel differential by about 5%, so the controller needs slightly more damping to avoid overshoot. Iteration 7 already shows the damping margin shrinking: s-bend steering_oscillation rose to 0.347 (from 0.304 at iteration 6), and iteration 2 overshot at 0.11 m with kp 4.0 and kd 0.3. I therefore keep kp at 3.8 and ki at 0.15 unchanged, and raise kd from 0.60 to 0.65 to damp the faster heading response. Sensor weights stay at x/0.015 (-2 to +2), so the signal remains sign-correct with positive meaning left. base_speed stays at 1.4, since oval and slalom finish times leave time margin, and line_loss stays last_direction, which has given about one event per run. Expected result, not yet measured: slalom finishes rise toward 16 or 17 of 20, slalom steering_oscillation stays at or below about 0.32, and oval and s-bend completions hold at 20/20 and 18/20 or better.
